title: A simultaneous reference can identify common gain drift
incomingEvidence: v3 S2B/S5A: exp(beta t) acquisition gain is exactly confounded with a shifted physical decay in a lone channel.
question: Under a shared scalar exponential acquisition gain, does a nondecaying simultaneous reference identify the target decay, and which physically different rival still survives?

model.target: x_s(t)=A_s exp((-alpha+beta_s)t) cos(2 pi f_s t + phi_s)
model.reference: x_r(t)=A_r exp(beta_r t) cos(2 pi f_r t + phi_r)
model.sharedGainPremise: beta_s=beta_r=beta; independently stable reference amplitude before receiver
model.observation: ideal separated channels followed by generated stereo PCM; this is not a one-microphone spectral separation claim

controls: differential gain beta_s=2,beta_r=1: expected corrected alpha=3
unstable reference: true reference alpha_r=1 with shared beta=2 gives same corrected bias
falsifier: Valid common-gain PCM fixtures exceed correction tolerance, or a claimed universal correction admits unstable/differential reference as identified intrinsic damping.
claimCeiling: Conditional parameter recovery in a stipulated shared-gain model and a implementable recording witness proposal; no calibrated material damping or physical result.
loopA: Producer executes frozen model and reports artifacts; no next-round execution.
loopB: Independent skeptic derives rank/kernel and reruns adversarial controls; producer repairs if needed; advisor admits narrowly then selects next question.
